title: Plymouth's ghost map: Menacing spirits and phantom pub drinkers
excerpt: Plymouth's creepiest paranormal secrets have been laid bare
content:
Phantom kitchen saboteurs, spectral soldiers, and Victorian children lingering in shopfronts are among thousands of apparitions reported to be haunting Britain’s towns and cities.

Author Dr Paul Lee has documented more than 5,500 reported hauntings around the country over a decade of painstaking research, and they are all included in our interactive map revealing Britain’s most haunted locations.

Reports range from everyday oddities – including phantom tobacco smoke and unexplained footsteps – to intense poltergeist claims involving flying plates and airborne kitchen utensils.

In Plymouth, there have been a number of super spooky sightings and paranormal encounters reported.

‌

A "White Lady", described as "menacing" wanders around the ruins at Budshead Manor, whilst there are stories of banging in the cellar, a figure sat at a table and a flash of light at The Ferry House Inn pub near the Tamar.

Further inland at The Britannia, shadows and silhouettes have been seen in the bar, before making their way to the toilets, 'one of these seems to be a 6 foot tall male with clothing dating back to the early 1900s.'

Over at Saltram House, the spirit of a hooded apparition who wanders the dining room and halls is said to be that of a kitchen maid who was murdered.

You can discover the haunted locations near you using our interactive map.

‌

According to Dr Lee’s research, Britain’s most haunted postcode is the ME1 neighbourhood, which covers Rochester, Burham, and Wouldham in Kent.

Paranormal experiences have been documented at more than 50 separate locations across these Medway communities.

Among them is the former Royal Function Rooms, an 18th-century theatre that closed in 2022. The venue was long said to be haunted by three separate spectres.

‌

They include an aggressive figure in an 18th-century waistcoat who allegedly ran across the stage overturning furniture, a second shouting phantom, and a woman in a bonnet who was reported to rattle door handles in the basement.

Nearby, at the historic St Bartholomew’s Hospital site, records describe chairs flying across consulting rooms, doctors’ coats being moved by unseen hands, and lights flicking on and off unassisted.

The site has also accumulated folklore of phantom children, an old woman walking through walls, and a talkative Cavalier.

‌

York City Centre (YO1) is the UK’s second most haunted postcode, and is rightly famous for its ghost walks.

One of the city's most chilling tales centres on St Saviour Church, where a "grey lady" is reputed to walk at midnight. Local folklore tells of an amateur ghost hunter who spent the night locked inside the church, only to be discovered the following morning either dead with his face a “mask of terror”, or scared out of his senses, depending on the retelling.

Other York apparitions include a phantom mourner who reportedly appears at funerals to stare at coffins, and “Mad Alice” who haunts the lane named in her honour.

Since Dr Lee started his research, a handful of haunted buildings that he documented no longer exist. However, the spooks described may still linger on.

‌

All the descriptions of paranormal activity on the map have come from Dr Lee’s meticulous research, which, in many cases, includes interviews with witnesses and his own investigations, during which he has visited numerous locations and trawled through various newspaper archives.

Dr Lee said: “Of course, some of the reports in the database could be hoaxes or urban legends; there is no way to know in many cases.”

Dr Lee, who holds a doctorate in nuclear physics, began compiling the national register in 2015 and continues to update the archive.

His recent investigations include the Syderstone Ghost — a series of unexplained night-time disturbances in a Norfolk village that was recently featured in Fortean Times.

‌

Dr Lee has published his findings in several volumes, including the UK Haunted Hospitality series, which investigates more than 2,000 haunted pubs, hotels, and eateries across the country.

You can find out more about his research by visiting his website: www.paullee.com/ghosts .
